items.headline: Iran and the US trade fire across the Gulf
items.summary: Iran says drones hit a US radar at Sheikh Isa air base in Bahrain, which Bahrain and CENTCOM say was intercepted. The US struck a missile site on Qeshm island, Kuwait reported drone attacks, and three tankers hit mines in Hormuz.
items.matters: the third Iranian drone attack on Bahrain in five days, with a third US carrier now in theatre, takes the standoff close to open war.
items.body:
x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info A still image from a social media video released on Tuesday shows a tanker on fire in the Strait of Hormuz, off the coast of Oman [Social media via Reuters] By Al Jazeera Staff and AFP Published On 17 Nov 2026 17 Nov 2026 Kuwait’s army has said the Gulf country is under attack by drones while the United States and Iran traded blows, marking escalating tensions in the region as a peace deal remains elusive.

The military said in a statement on X on Tuesday that “any explosion sounds heard are the result of air defence systems intercepting hostile attacks”.

The US earlier carried out several attacks on Iran’s southern island of Qeshm, in the Strait of Hormuz, hours after Iran said it launched a drone attack on a US radar system in Bahrain.

“The American attack on locations on Qeshm island caused no damage to residential, commercial, or infrastructural areas,” Ahmad Nafisi, deputy governor of Iran’s southern Hormozgan province, told the official IRNA news agency on Tuesday.

He said the situation was under control and relief agencies were on full alert. IRNA reported five to six explosions on the island on Tuesday evening.

A US official told Al Jazeera the strike hit a missile launch site on Qeshm, in response to Iran’s earlier attack on a US base in Bahrain.

US Central Command said Iranian drones aimed at a US radar system at an air base in Bahrain “were intercepted without any damage to US equipment or personnel”.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it carried out a “precision operation” with drones on the US-operated radar at the Sheikh Isa air base, in response to “repeated violations of Iranian airspace by US military drones”.

Bahrain, which hosts the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, said its air defences intercepted the attack, and blasts were heard over the capital, Manama, according to the AFP news agency.

It was the third Iranian drone attack on Bahrain in five days after a lull of several weeks. Friday’s strike was the first Iranian attack on a Gulf country since early September, AFP reported. Reuters said it came after a Bahraini court sentenced 64 people, mostly Shia clerics, to life in prison for allegedly colluding with Iran.

Kuwait’s armed forces said on Tuesday night that its air defences were responding to “hostile drone attacks” and urged the public to follow safety instructions.

It did not say where the drones came from or whether there were casualties or damage.

items.headline: Mary Peltola flips Alaska and gives Democrats a 56-44 Senate
items.summary: the AP called the last contest of the cycle on Tuesday night, a nine-seat gain and the biggest since 1958. The Justice Department had sued to decertify the result if the Republican incumbent lost, and legal challenges are expected.
items.matters: the midterm result is settled on the numbers but not yet in the courts.
items.body:
x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info Democratic US Senate candidate Mary Peltola speaks during an election night rally for the US midterm elections in Anchorage, Alaska, on November 3, 2026 [File: Kerry Tasker/Reuters] By Al Jazeera Staff and The Associated Press Published On 18 Nov 2026 18 Nov 2026 Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan in the race for Alaska’s Senate seat, delivering a final blow to Republicans in a midterm election rout following a race that drew accusations of cheating.

The Associated Press (AP) news agency called the race on Tuesday night, capping a contest that attracted national attention after an investigation alleged that aides to Peltola recruited another man named Dan Sullivan to run for office to siphon votes from the Republican incumbent.

Sullivan had pledged to accept the election outcome days after the Department of Justice filed a lawsuit seeking to decertify the results if the Republican incumbent lost.

Alaska also elected a Democrat as governor for the first time since 1998, after former state lawmaker Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins defeated three Republicans, including one endorsed by US President Donald Trump. AP has not yet called the US House race, where independent candidate Bill Hill is challenging Republican Representative Nick Begich.

The Alaska race is the last US Senate contest to be resolved in this year’s midterm elections, and Peltola’s victory expands the Democrats’ majority after they retook control of the chamber. The party already won campaigns in conservative states including South Carolina, Texas, Kansas and, most recently, Mississippi.

With Peltola’s victory, Democrats flipped nine Senate seats, the most since 1958. Republicans entered the midterms with a 53-47 majority, while Democrats now emerge with a 56-44 margin.

Peltola previously held the state’s lone House seat, making her the first Alaska Native to serve in Congress. She lost her bid for a second full term to Begich in 2024, but she became central to Democrats’ plans to retake the Senate in 2026.

During the campaign, Peltola tapped into Alaskans’ frustrations with high fuel prices and other costs. Those concerns hit especially hard in remote communities that rely on diesel for electricity and heat and are often only accessible by air or water.

Her campaign peppered social media with photos of her travels around the state as she sought to distance herself from national Democrats and build a coalition around a platform of “Alaska first”.

items.headline: The US-backed Board of Peace warns the Gaza ceasefire faces imminent collapse
items.summary: its report to the UN Security Council blames Israeli aid restrictions and the blocked civil administration and police deployment. It also says both sides have fallen far short of their commitments.
items.matters: the body Trump created to run the truce is now saying publicly that it is failing, a year after it began on 10 October 2025.
items.body:
x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info Palestinians walk past displacement tents in Khan Yunis in the southern Gaza Strip on November 17, 2026 [Eyad Baba / AFP] By Al Jazeera Staff and The Associated Press Published On 18 Nov 2026 18 Nov 2026 The United States-backed Board of Peace has delivered a grim assessment to the United Nations Security Council, warning diplomats of conditions that threaten the year-old truce in war-torn Gaza.

In its latest report, submitted on Tuesday, the board cautioned that, without immediate steps to implement the 2025 ceasefire deal, the truce between Israel and Hamas may be on the brink of collapse.

“The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains the principal risk to the process,” the report said, which The Associated Press obtained.

The Board of Peace was created in 2025, at US President Donald Trump’s behest, to oversee the ceasefire deal and reconstruction in Gaza.

Since October 2023, the narrow coastal territory has been the target of a genocidal war carried out by Israel, which has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians.

In recent weeks, Israel has continued to carry out deadly air strikes, and its ongoing restrictions have prevented the delivery of life-saving aid into Gaza ahead of the winter season.

“Restrictions imposed by Israel on the entry of supplies and equipment, compounded by funding shortfalls, continued to impede preparedness and response efforts,” the board said in its report.

According to the board, the widespread devastation in Gaza has left Palestinians facing “another winter in tents and rubble”.

Trump first proposed the Board of Peace in September 2025, saying it would stabilise Gaza and ensure lasting peace.

The board’s mission was laid out in a 20-point Gaza peace plan, as well as the ceasefire between Israel and Hamas. The ceasefire formally began on October 10, 2025, though attacks have continued since.

The plan envisioned steps for each side to take that could eventually create a “credible pathway” to Palestinian statehood.

But in Tuesday’s report, the board said Israel and Hamas have fallen far short of their commitments in the ceasefire deal.

The board also noted that Israel has blocked the technocratic civil administration body created to run Gaza on an interim basis.

items.headline: Banki przestają liczyć 800+ do zdolności kredytowej

items.matters: rodzina z dziećmi może dostać o kilkadziesiąt tysięcy złotych mniejszy kredyt, choć KNF mówił, że nie oczekuje całkowitego wycofania.
items.body:
Skomentuj Nawet kilkadziesiąt tysięcy złotych kredytu mniej przez jedną decyzję – banki przestają akceptować 800+ jako czynnik wpływający na zdolność kredytową. Mało kto jednak pamięta, że banki zainteresowały się świadczeniem wychowawczym dość niedawno i w specyficznych okolicznościach.

fot. Tupungato / / Shutterstock Jest rok 2022. Program „Rodzina 500+” ma już za sobą 6 lat działania. Co miesiąc osoby wychowujące nieletnie dzieci otrzymują 500 zł na każdego potomka. To czynnik, który ustabilizował budżety wielu gospodarstw domowych, chociaż siła nabywcza świadczenia w międzyczasie mocno spadła.

Tymczasem na rynku kredytowym trwa „hipoteczna zima”. Stopy procentowe rosną, a kredyty hipoteczne gwałtownie drożeją. W takich okolicznościach nie dziwi, że zdolność kredytowa leci na łeb, na szyję. Para mająca do dyspozycji 6,2 tys. zł miesięcznie w połowie 2021 r. mogła liczyć na ponad pół miliona złotych finansowania. Rok później – ledwo na 280 tys. zł kredytu hipotecznego.

Banki poszukują sposobu podbicia zdolności kredytowej klientów. Pojawia się innowacja – kredytodawcy zaczynają uwzględniać „500 plus” w wyliczaniu finansowej wydolności kredytobiorców. „Świadczenie 500+ na jedno dziecko podnosi zdolność 3-osobowej rodziny o kilkanaście tysięcy złotych” – szacują wówczas eksperci Expandera. Pierwsze nowe podejście wdrażają banki PKO BP oraz Bank Pekao, chociaż nie chwalą się tym publicznie. W lipcu 2022 r. spośród 13 instytucji aktywnych na rynku, zaledwie 3 uwzględniały 500+ w obliczeniach.

W kolejnych miesiącach następne banki, sięgają po „dopalacz”. Podejście jest niejednolite. Bywa, że świadczenie powiększa dochód do dyspozycji, a czasem obniża koszty utrzymania kredytobiorcy. Różnie formułowane są także warunki wstępne, chociażby dotyczące zbieżności okresu kredytowania i okresu otrzymywania świadczenia. Wkrótce praktyka podbijania zdolności przez 500+ staje się rynkowym standardem, ale nadal mocno różni się w szczegółach.

Przeskoczmy do połowy 2026 r. Program 500+ doczekał się w międzyczasie aktualizacji – beneficjenci otrzymują już po 800 zł na dziecko. Nadal większość banków uwzględnia ten element w wyliczeniach zdolności kredytowej. Pod koniec czerwca na stronie Komisji Nadzoru Finansowego pojawia się wpis pod tytułem „Ocena zdolności kredytowej a świadczenie „Rodzina 800 plus” – czego oczekuje UKNF?”.

W treści znajdziemy szereg wskazówek dotyczących technicznych aspektów uwzględniania 800+ w szacowaniu wydolności klienta. „Są to dochody, których stabilność zależy od wieku dziecka, na które świadczenie przysługuje i których okres…

items.headline: Wall Street fell as chips slid before Nvidia reported
items.summary: the Dow lost 1.64% (over 800 points) to 50,759.42, the S&P 500 1.03% to 7,340.53 and the Nasdaq 0.74% to 24,328.38.
items.matters: this is the selloff that Nvidia's results were due to answer, and Brent closed at $92.82.
items.body:
Skomentuj Wtorkowa sesja na Wall Street zakończyła się sporymi spadkami głównych indeksów, a Dow Jones zniżkował ponad 800 pkt. Wyprzedaż akcji producentów półprzewodników przed publikacją kwartalnych wyników Nvidii ciążyła indeksowi Nasdaq Composite.

fot. Christian Reister / imageBROKER / / FORUM Dow Jones Industrial na zamknięciu spadł o 1,64 proc. i wyniósł 50.759,42 pkt.

Indeks spółek o średniej kapitalizacji Russell 2000 spada o 1,4 proc. i wynosi 2.704,4 pkt.

We wtorek po sesji raport finansowy za III kw. przedstawi spółka Nvidia. Według danych LSEG analitycy przewidują wzrost zysków o 90 proc. przy przychodach wynoszących 109 mld dolarów w trzecim kwartale roku obrotowego spółki.

"W oczekiwaniu na wyniki finansowe Nvidii nie ulega wątpliwości, że na kierunek notowań spółki wpłynie to, kto zostanie jej kolejnym dyrektorem generalnym (...), a także skala negatywnego wpływu zmian w polityce Stanów Zjednoczonych na działalność Nvidii w Chinach, zarówno bezpośrednią, jak i pośrednią. Uważam jednak, że najważniejszym czynnikiem będzie ogólny poziom nakładów inwestycyjnych w branży" – napisał Peter Boockvar, dyrektor inwestycyjny One Point BFG Wealth Partners.

"Akcje Nvidii spadają nie tylko z powodu odejścia Jensena Huanga i wzmożonej kontroli dotyczącej działalności spółki w Chinach. Ostatecznie Nvidia jest również jednym z dostawców infrastruktury niezbędnej do rozbudowy centrów danych, a obserwowaliśmy już, co stało się z notowaniami wielu podobnych spółek; ich akcje gwałtownie potaniały" – dodał.

Odejście Jensena Huanga ze stanowiska prezesa Nvidii w zeszłym tygodniu skierowało uwagę na wyniki firmy, z powodu obaw o obniżenie marż i odpływ gotówki, biorąc pod uwagę ogromny wpływ firmy na ekosystem sztucznej inteligencji.

"Zyski i sytuacja po odejściu Jensena Huanga to nie jedyne punkty zainteresowania w dzisiejszym wieczornym raporcie finansowym. Inwestorzy chcą również wiedzieć, jak długo cykl nakładów inwestycyjnych największych spółek technologicznych utrzyma wzrost sprzedaży Nvidii" – powiedziała Kathleen Brooks, dyrektorka ds. analiz w XTB.

"Wyniki finansowe będą bardzo mocne. Nie musi to jednak stanowić wsparcia dla rynku, zwłaszcza że dzieje się obecnie tak wiele innych rzeczy" – powiedział Neil Wilson, strateg w Saxo UK.

Agencja Reutera podała, powołując się na trzy źródła, że zarząd Nvidii nie rozważa powrotu założyciela na stanowisko prezesa w związku z kampanią na rzecz jego przywrócenia na stanowisko, która zyskała poparcie Elona Muska i innych osobistości z Doliny Krzemowej. Huang zrezygnował ze stanowiska w zeszłym tygodniu…

items.body:
Skomentuj Po pięciu z rzędu wzrostowych sesjach i poniedziałkowym ustanowieniu historycznych szczytów na GPW przyszła wyraźna korektora. Wtorkowe notowania upłynęły pod znakiem szerokiej realizacji zysków oraz potężnej wyprzedaży akcji XTB po zapowiedziach Komisji Nadzoru Finansowego.

/ Ilustracja wygenerowana przy użyciu AI Na zamknięciu wtorkowej sesji WIG20 spadł o 1,16 proc., a indeks szerokiego rynku WIG zniżkował o 1,48 proc. Na zapleczu największych spółek – mWIG40 poszedł w dół o 2,68 proc., natomiast sWIG80 stracił 1,44 proc. Obroty na szerokim rynku wyniosły 2,43 mld zł, przy czym 1,63 mld zł dotyczyło handlu akcjami spółek z WIG20, ale rekord dziennych obrotów dotyczył spółki XTB z mWIG40 (417,3 mln zł).

Wtorkowa korekta przerwała imponującą passę pięciu sesji, kiedy WIG20 rósł bez przerwy, zyskując łącznie ponad 4 proc. W poniedziałek indeks największych spółek wyznaczył nowe historyczne maksimum na poziomie 4.321,54 pkt. oraz rekord na zamknięciu. Analogicznie zachowywał się WIG, śrubując w poniedziałek zarówno rekord wszech czasów w trakcie notowań (162.596,49 pkt.), jak i najwyższy kurs zamknięcia w historii.

Słabość warszawskiego parkietu wpisywała się w szerszy, globalny odwrót od ryzykownych aktywów. Wcześniej spadki zdominowały giełdy w Azji, a w momencie zakończenia sesji w Warszawie wyraźnie pod kreską znajdowały się najważniejsze indeksy w Europie. Niemiecki DAX tracił 2,2 proc., brytyjski FTSE 100 spadał o 1,8 proc., a francuski CAC40 zniżkował o 1,6 proc. Około 1,5-procentowe przeceny obserwowano na parkietach w Madrycie, Mediolanie, Amsterdamie oraz Zurychu.

Równie nerwowo rozpoczęła się sesja za oceanem, gdzie S&P 500 tracił 1,1 proc., a technologiczny Nasdaq spadał o 1,4 proc. Inwestorzy w USA wstrzymywali oddech przed publikacją wyników finansowych Nvidii oraz planowanym debiutem spółki Anthropic. Nastroje wokół sektora sztucznej inteligencji chłodziły obawy o rentowność wielomiliardowych nakładów na centra danych, a oliwy do ognia dolało Amerykańskie Biuro Przemysłu i Bezpieczeństwa (BIS), ogłaszając nowe ograniczenia w dostępie chińskich firm do zaawansowanych układów AI.

Rynkom nie pomogły też publikacje makroekonomiczne z USA – październikowa sprzedaż detaliczna potwierdziła wyhamowanie dynamiki zgodnie z oczekiwaniami, jednak negatywnie zaskoczyły słabsze od prognoz dane o produkcji przemysłowej, co tylko lekko skorygowało siłę amerykańskiego dolara.

Od strony technicznej wtorkowe cofnięcie w Warszawie oddaliło scenariusz natychmiastowego wybicia górą. Jak zauważa Przemysław Smoliński, analityk BM PKO BP, podaż…

items.headline: The government will decide in coming weeks whether to extend the CPN fuel package into 2027
items.summary: Finance Minister Domański says it costs about 1.6bn zł a month, more than the windfall tax on fuel companies brings in.
items.matters: the package expires at year-end, and its VAT and excise cuts keep pump prices near the 2025 average.
items.body:
Skomentuj W najbliższych tygodniach rząd podejmie decyzję, czy pakiet Ceny Paliwa Niżej powinien być w całości lub częściowo przedłużony w pierwszych miesiącach 2027 r. - poinformował minister finansów i gospodarki Andrzej Domański. Obecnie CPN ma działać jedynie do końca roku.

We wtorek Domański na antenie TVN24 dopytywany był o rządowy program CPN, który obniża ceny paliw na stacjach benzynowych.

Domański przyznał, że obecnie nie zapadła jeszcze decyzja o ewentualnym przedłużeniu programu, choć rząd prowadzi analizy. Poinformował jednocześnie, że „myśli”, iż decyzje o tym, czy CPN powinien być w całości lub częściowo przedłużony również w pierwszych miesiącach 2027 r. to kwestia „najbliższych tygodni”.

- To jest pakiet, który kosztuje 1,6 mld zł miesięcznie. To są poważne, wysokie kwoty. (...) Ten pakiet kosztował budżet więcej niż przychody z podatku od nadmiarowych zysków (koncernów paliwowych) - zauważył minister.

Ocenił też, że obecnie ceny na stacjach, dzięki programowi CPN, są obecnie „na poziomie zbliżonym do średniej, którą widzieliśmy w 2025 r., czyli przed wybuchem konfliktu na Bliskim Wschodzie”.

items.headline: Nvidia posts $115.8bn and guides $130bn in its first quarter without Jensen Huang
items.summary: revenue roughly doubled on the year against about $109bn expected, net income rose 105% to $65.3bn, and the fourth-quarter guide of $130bn ±3% beat the Street, with shares up more than 5% after hours.
items.matters: Interim CEO Colette Kress also raised fiscal 2028 growth to about 75% and said Nvidia will be less generous with investments and guarantees to AI customers.
items.body:
Nvidia raised its sales forecast for its next fiscal year, and reported stronger-than-expected results in its most recent quarter, in a striking signal of business confidence by the AI chipmaker following the resignation of longtime CEO and cofounder Jensen Huang.

“Our momentum is real,” interim CEO Colette Kress said on conference call with analysts on Tuesday, citing strong demand for the company’s products, Nvidia’s ongoing technological advances, and the commitment of its employees. Kress, Nvidia’s longtime finance chief, made her debut as interim CEO on Tuesday’s earnings call, flanked by newly appointed chair of the board Harvey Jones.

The pair took pains to project a business-as-usual attitude—even using the phrase—while seeking to put Huang in the rear-view mirror. The board of directors “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO,” Jones said at the start of the call, noting that the company has retained executive recruiting firm Hedrick & Struggles to search for a permanent CEO.

The comments were a direct rebuttal to Huang, who is seeking to reclaim the CEO throne just days after resigning amid revelations of multiple affairs, one reportedly with a Nvidia employee who reported to him and another with a woman some believe may be a Chinese spy.

Shares of Nvidia were up more than 5% in after hours trading on Tuesday. The company’s stock has plummeted more than 36% in the past month, shedding more than a trillion dollars in market value.

Investors have been spooked by the loss of Nvidia’s longtime leader, Huang, as well as by general concerns about the durability of the AI boom. Kress doused both concerns at once on Tuesday by raising sales expectations for Nvidia’s fiscal 2028 year, which is roughly equivalent to the 2027 calendar year.

“We had originally indicated that we would be at about 70% growth year-over-year, and now we are are increasing that to 75%” growth,” Kress said, citing improvements in supply and ongoing strength in demand. The guidance was particularly striking because Huang himself had delivered the 70% growth forecast three months ago, framing it as an usually far-reaching forecast that reflected the exceptional strength in the business.

In raising the annual revenue forecast by the equivalent of $20 billion or more, Nvidia’s message seemed to be that Huang was not so essential after all. “We got this,” Kress said during the call.

“The quarter answers the first question the market had about Nvidia without its founder: demand did not leave with him,” Dan Ives, a partner and analyst at Yorkville Ives, wrote in a note to…

items.headline: Nvidia's board puts chip exports under a new oversight committee
items.summary: the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, chaired by Suzanne Nora Johnson, meets at least quarterly and takes reports from compliance and Kress, after Huang's exit over the Megaspeed diversion questions.
items.matters: export control is now a board-level risk at the company that supplies the AI buildout.
items.body:
Nvidia's board has created a national security and export control committee amid intense scrutiny over co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang's departure and allegations that Singapore-based customer Megaspeed diverted GPUs to China.

The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, announced on Tuesday, will monitor Nvidia's national security policies, export compliance, and global trade risks. It will meet at least quarterly.

The committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson and include directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members. Nvidia's existing National Security and Global Trade Compliance teams will report on day-to-day operations directly to this new committee, as well as to interim CEO Colette Kress.

The panel will oversee efforts to strengthen Nvidia's national security and trade compliance teams and retain independent legal, national security, and trade experts.

The announcement follows the resignation of Huang last week after he admitted to an affair with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive, and was allegedly involved in a second relationship with an Nvidia employee.

US authorities reportedly suspected Alice Huang of working for Chinese intelligence, an allegation that has not been proven. Megaspeed has separately faced scrutiny over suspected export control violations.

The US Department of Commerce and Department of Justice confirmed on Tuesday in a joint statement that they were investigating Megaspeed back in 2024. The agencies said they would pursue any criminal conduct uncovered by the investigation.

However, Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs stated that US authorities had provided only "limited assistance" when they were investigating the activities of Alice Huang and Megaspeed, as The Register reported.

The New York Times also reported that US investigations into Megaspeed were halted last year after an Nvidia executive contacted Commerce Department officials.

The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has issued new regulations tightening up restrictions on AI technology exports and cloud operators offering remote access to it.

The US also expanded its Pax Silica initiative, getting allied nations to sign an agreement that "guarding AI supply chains" is a shared responsibility.

Nvidia says it recognizes that advanced silicon and AI technologies present challenges for national security, and it has a responsibility to address them.

items.headline: Oracle discloses "Java4Shell", a 9.2 critical OpenJDK flaw
items.summary: CVE-2026-114938 is a memory-corruption bug in the optimised x86-64 Base64 decoder, reachable before authentication in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Kafka and Elasticsearch, and CISA urges immediate patching.
items.matters: until you patch, start the JVM with AVX-512 disabled; Cisco Talos expects probing to rise after disclosure.
items.body:
Oracle revealed the flaw in its monthly patch dump for November, which offers 655 patches, 62 of them rated critical, affecting 62 products.

Several of the flaws are rated more dangerous than the Java problem, CVE-2026-114938, which Big Red didn’t single out as worthy of special attention despite CISA’s warning.

The cyber-agency’s decision seems apt because vulnerability research and red teaming outfit Calif.io, which discovered the flaw, used its X account to claim news of the problem had leaked before public disclosure and the release of Oracle's fixes.

By then, Calif had already tested the flaw, which it named “Java4Shell,” and found applications including Keycloak, Atlassian’s Jira and Confluence, Jenkins, Apache Kafka Broker, and Elasticsearch are susceptible to RCE.

Calif, which also helped to find the PHP2Shell flaw, says the flaw is a memory-corruption vulnerability in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder.

Calif applied the CVSS 4.0 bug-rating scheme and gave the flaw a critical-rated score of 9.2/10.

Cisco’s Talos security team pointed out that the flaw is present in OpenJDK Java versions 17.0.6 and later running on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions) support enabled.

“These vulnerabilities have already been tested against a suite of Java applications with success, but the attack surface is likely much larger as additional targets are tested and confirmed,” Talos advised.

Cisco’s infosec experts urged adoption of the fixed versions of Java Oracle posted on Tuesday but noted it is possible to mitigate the flaw on x86-64 machines by starting the JVM with support for AVX-512 disabled.

Akamai’s Chief Information Security Architect Jan Schaumann, writing on the Openwall project’s mailing list, expressed a little discomfort with Calif’s work.

That second sentence perhaps supports Calif’s assertion that news of the flaw leaked before disclosure.

So do the six 10.10 flaws Oracle reported, three in its Access Manager product, one in the Oracle Platform Security for Java, another in the WebLogic Server, and one in Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition.

By Tenable Security’s count, 249 of the patches are for high severity bugs. Oracle’s Hyperion enterprise performance management accounts for 267 of the bugs.

items.headline: Uber confirms the Fireworks AI breach exposed 149,346 drivers' licence records
items.summary: attackers used valid credentials on Uber's dedicated storage on 7 October, and Fireworks has since admitted a second breach that reached billing records, customer datasets and incomplete model weights.
items.matters: an AI inference vendor holding identity documents is a supply-chain risk, and Uber's notices only began on 10 November.
items.body:
Uber has confirmed that nearly 150,000 people had their personal information compromised after hackers broke into one of its AI suppliers.

A filing with Oregon's attorney general puts the number of victims at 149,346. Among the data the crooks got their hands on were images of drivers' licenses and information extracted from them, including names, home addresses, dates of birth, and license numbers.

Uber doesn't name the supplier in its filings with US state attorneys general, but told TechCrunch it was Fireworks AI, the inference outfit whose security woes we covered last week.

According to a breach notification filed with Iowa's attorney general, Fireworks alerted Uber to the intrusion on October 9. Uber cut off the supplier's access to its data and, four days later, established that the attackers had accessed drivers' personal information on October 7.

Uber had set up a dedicated cloud storage environment for the AI biz, complete with security monitoring overseen by its own cloud security team. Unfortunately for Uber and its drivers, the crooks were using legitimate credentials, so none of the alarms went off.

The ride-hailing firm says those credentials couldn't be used to access its other systems, and says it has since revoked or changed the credentials associated with the supplier.

Uber hasn't said why it handed images of thousands of driver's licenses to an AI inference outfit. The Register has put that question to both companies, and asked Uber if any drivers outside the US had their data exposed.

Fireworks, which provides infrastructure for developers to run and fine-tune AI models, had a particularly miserable October. The company first disclosed a security incident on October 9 after discovering that someone had been using its internal credentials without permission.

Fireworks initially said it had no evidence that the intruders had gotten their hands on personal information or customer datasets. The company was hacked again later that month and, on November 9, disclosed that some customer data had indeed been compromised.

The AI biz acknowledged that attackers had accessed billing records, some customer datasets, and incomplete model weights. Productivity software maker Notion was among those affected, with some of its customers' conversations with its AI assistant exposed.

Fireworks suspects the involvement of financially motivated criminals in the business of flogging unauthorized access to large language models. Whether the crooks have any plans for the haul of Uber drivers' personal information is unclear.

items.headline: A run of outages hits critical systems
items.summary: Microsoft 365 mail and Intune went down on 12 November, the FAA grounded planes on 13 November, Chase, Bank of America and US Bank had problems on 16 November, and yesterday the NSA's NSANet and Apple services (iCloud, App Store, Apple Pay) went offline.
items.matters: none of the five is attributed to a cyberattack, and Satya Nadella opened Ignite by apologising for the Microsoft 365 failure.
items.body:
NSA, Apple add to a week of high-profile network outages, largely attributed to 'routine maintenance'

Another day, another disruptive network outage (or two) as government officials and company execs scramble to assure an anxious populace that these are not coordinated cyberattacks – and security experts call this the new normal.

Around the same time, Apple users began reporting issues across multiple services – including Apple Support, iCloud, the App Store, Apple Pay, and more – with Apple retail stores worldwide also reportedly experiencing disruptions that halted sales and in-person support.

All of these high-profile outages followed last week’s US Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) order g rounding all planes on Friday due to problems with copper wiring during an L3Harris network upgrade, and a Microsoft 365 outage on Thursday.

Redmond later blamed the massive service disruption on a faulty software update it pushed back in July.

Despite the weekend respite from network outages, your humble vulture still had to field is-this-the-beginning-of-the-end questions from friends and family all day Saturday and Sunday, most of whom suspected Russia or China – maybe even Iran – caused the spate of downed systems and services.

A highly sophisticated, coordinated nation-state hack would be a much more exciting cause for the disruptions. The real culprit, however, appears to be aging, under-funded infrastructure, riddled with decades-old bugs and held together by digital sticks and glue.

“As someone who started out as a hacker, I know how tempting it is to connect the dots when major systems fail one after another,” Remedio CEO Tal Kollender told The Register, adding that there’s “no credible public evidence that these outages were part of a coordinated cyberattack,” and most have been attributed to technical failures.

For people who couldn’t withdraw money from their bank, board a flight, or use email at work on Friday, “the disruption was real regardless of the cause,” she said.

Then we go and add AI to this already delicate balance, and everything essentially blows up.

AI-assisted bug hunting and exploit development has surfaced more than 100,000 CVEs so far this year, with Microsoft’s Patch Tuesday disclosing more than 1,000 vulnerabilities in each of the past two months. items.headline: NuGet.org introduces staged publishing
items.summary: packages are validated privately and stay hidden from search and restore until an authorised maintainer promotes them with two-factor authentication, and staging-only pipeline credentials cannot publish directly.
items.matters: it is opt-in, group promotion is not atomic, and the .NET 11 RC2 SDK can stage with `dotnet package stage push`, so any plugin library you publish can get a safer release gate.
items.body:
A successful build tells you that your pipeline finished. It does not tell you that you meant to release. Today, we are introducing staged publishing on NuGet.org, available to all package publishers, so you can prepare and validate packages privately before making an explicit decision to publish them.

Upload a security fix ahead of its coordinated disclosure. Gather the packages for a feature release without exposing an unfinished set. Let automation prepare a large update, then review it on NuGet.org before it reaches the people who depend on it.

With a normal package push, upload starts the public publishing process. Staged publishing adds a place to stop: the package goes through NuGet.org validation, but stays private until an authorized maintainer promotes it through the website.

That gives you time to review what you are about to ship, fix validation problems, and choose the release moment.

Staging is opt-in. Existing dotnet nuget push workflows continue to work. You can adopt staging for a security-sensitive package or a coordinated release without changing every publishing workflow at once.

Staging also differs from unlisting. An unlisted package can still be restored by its exact version. A staged package is not available to consumers at all.

The website is where you review staged content and approve its release. You can stage a single package or organize related packages into a staging group.

On the NuGet.org upload page, choose the staging option under Publishing Mode when uploading your package. You can also upload from your pipeline using the CLI example below.

NuGet.org runs the package through its validation pipeline, including malware scanning, signature checks, and repository signing. Once validation succeeds, the package is ready for promotion. It stays out of public package pages, search results, and restore operations.

You can inspect the staged package and its validation status in the website’s package management experience. If validation fails, fix the problem and stage a replacement before release day.

Staging does not provide a private restore feed, even for the owner. Test your packages and their dependencies using a local or private feed first, then stage the release artifacts on NuGet.org.

A staging group collects the packages for a release under one staging owner, either a user or an organization. For example, a library, its integrations, and its analyzers can share a group for an upcoming feature release.

items.matters: this is the first enforcement answer to the week's streamer-farming row, but Blizzard gave no suspension numbers and named nobody.
items.body:
As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced. Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.

Over the past weekend, some players discovered a large group of non-elite enemies in the Blackmaw Hold dungeon that were incorrectly dropping the full amount of dungeon loot that would be expected from an elite. Early yesterday, we addressed this with a hotfix, and since then, we have been investigating the overall economic impact.

Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug. But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies.

Yesterday, we put an economy lock on their accounts to prevent broader impact to the game economy while we investigated the extent of the exploitative gains, including gold earned by vendoring bugged drops. Today, we are in the process of removing all such gold earned, as well as applying account suspensions to significant abusers.

As always, we advise all players to refrain from abusing game mechanics that are clearly unintended. We will continue to take action against intentional abuse.

items.headline: King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard announced Entropy for 4 December
items.summary: their 29th album arrives on their own p(doom) records, with lead single "Rogue Wave" and a 2027 tour that includes Primavera Sound.
items.matters: a second electronic-leaning record in a year and a tour that runs from Europe in June to North America in August and October.
items.body:
[Updated 11/10/26 5:30 ET]: King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard confirmed in an email to fans that they will not host Field of Vision III in Buena Vista, CO next year, saying “ Meadow Creek and Chaffee County were unable to agree upon permit conditions …” In the same email, the band announced four additional shows on its 2027 North American tour—three in Colorado and one in Reno, Nevada.

The new shows will take place on Friday, August 13th at Ford Amphitheater in Colorado Springs; Saturday, August 14th at Mission Ballroom in Denver; Sunday, August 15th at Dillon Amphitheater in Dillon; and Tuesday, August 17th at Club Underground in Reno.

Due out December 4th via their own p(doom) records label, Entropy is a companion album to Gizz’s last release, Alien Metal, from earlier this year. The new LP was born from the same experimental sessions where the band explored its Eurorack modular synth setup, affectionately referred to as “Nathan,” which has become the focal point of the group’s live rave sets.

Though the two albums share the same DNA, each emerged from a different improvised jam. Whereas Alien Metal ’s tracks were all set to a tempo of 143 beats per minute and in the key of F sharp, Entropy ’s pick up the pace to 160 bpm and are all in the key of A, giving each project its own distinct vibe.

Check out “Rogue Wave,” the first single from the forthcoming album, below or on your preferred streaming platform. Scroll down to view the full Entropy tracklist.

items.headline: Chvrches' All The King's Men lands 22 January
items.summary: their first album in almost six years, 11 tracks led by "Roses", with 27 tour dates from 13 February in Philadelphia to 6 May at London's O2 Shepherd's Bush Empire.
items.matters: the comeback has a fixed date and a tour that runs through North America, the UK and Ireland.
items.body:
Chvrches have announced their new album, All The King’s Men, alongside a 2027 tour that will take them across North America, the UK, and Ireland early next year.

All The King’s Men marks their first album in almost six years and is set to arrive on January 22nd, 2027, and follows on from their 2021 full-length, Screen Violence.

The trio, consisting of Lauren Mayberry, Iain Cook and Martin Doherty, have returned with “a self-consciously British freewheeling collection of 11 tracks of vividly emotional indie rock that fans won’t expect,” press materials promise.

The musicians have been inspired by a wide array of multidisciplinary art, such as Massive Attack, Souxsie and The Banshees, and PJ Harvey, as well as Nick Drake, Bert Jansch and Incredible String Band, and even British cinema auteurs like Shane Meadows and Ken Loach.

They have already released the first single, ‘Roses’, an Orwellian growl at the darker undercurrents of British society, which only “sets the stage for what is to come”.

The group has also announced a huge show of North America, the UK and Ireland kicking off next February 13th in Philadelphia and concluding on May 6th at London’s O2 Shepherd’s Bush Empire.

First, the trio will perform two special intimate shows in their hometown, Glasgow, on October 26th and in London on October 29th.

items.summary: RAYE tops the bill on 3 July in Gdynia, with Tame Impala opening the festival on 30 June and sombr and Patti Smith on 1 July.
items.matters: RAYE, who leads this year's Grammy nominations with 11, is already booked for the Polish festival.
items.body:
Sobel i OKI od ponad pół dekady zachwycają słuchaczy swoimi kolaboracjami. Chociaż wspólny album jeszcze przed nimi, już teraz z ich wydanych razem utworami można by złożyć solidną playlistę, pokazującą ewolucję obu artystów.

Na tę informację czekali europejscy fani U2! Zespół podzielił się swoimi koncertowymi planami i wstępnie zapowiada przedłużenie trasy na 2028 rok!

NOW > Muzyka > Oto nowe ogłoszenia na Open’er Festival! Kto wystąpi w 2027 roku?

Zaskoczenia, różnorodność, a przede wszystkim solidna dawka dźwiękowych wrażeń – to właśnie te składniki od lat budują Open’er Festival! Impreza od lat cieszy się ogromną popularnością wśród kilku pokoleń zagorzałych fanów muzyki, a line-up nieustannie przeplata wiele gatunków, co idealnie nasyci oczekiwania poszukiwaczy nowego brzmienia. Na scenach przez lata prezentowały się zarówno ponadczasowe legendy, jak i początkujący artyści, którzy dopiero rozwijali swoje twórcze skrzydła. Festiwalowicze co roku przywożą z Gdyni masę wspomnień i mają ochotę na więcej!

O tym, że Tame Impala rozkręci imprezę w Gdyni, wiemy już od pewnego czasu, ale entuzjazm wokół ogłoszenia nadal nie maleje. Projekt Kevina Parkera cieszy się ogromną popularnością w naszym kraju, o czym świadczy wysoka frekwencja na jego dwóch koncertach w Gliwicach, które odbyły się w 2026 roku. Tym razem Australijczyk nastroi fanów w festiwalową atmosferę, a pomoże mu w tym jego repertuar, który aż zaprasza do tańca! Więcej przeczytacie tutaj.

“Nic nie jest w stanie przygotować cię na sukces” – powiedział sombr w wywiadzie z Billboardem, gdy piosenka “back to friends” wkroczyła na nową falę popularności. Młody wokalista zderzył się z ogromnym uznaniem również w naszym kraju, ponieważ jego pierwszy koncert w Polsce od razu zyskał status sold-outu. Tym razem autor wielu przebojów będzie miał szansę rozkochać w sobie o wiele większą publiczność, a jego set z pewnością będzie motywem, by wielu entuzjastów popu zawitało do Gdyni w 2027 roku.

“back to friends”, “undressed”, “12 to 12” to zaledwie zalążek tego, co ma do zaprezentowania wokalista! Niedawno wzbogacił swój muzyczny katalog o single “Potential” oraz “My Body Isn’t Ready “, więc całkiem prawdopodobne, że te kawałki już wkrótce wybrzmią na festiwalu! sombr łączy w sobie indie-popową wrażliwość oraz chwytliwe melodie, który znalazły solidne grono entuzjastów w różnych częściach świata. Jego nadchodząca trasa koncertowa odbędzie się pod szyldem “You Are The Reason”, więc kto wie – może artysta ma w zanadrzu nowy repertuar, który zaprezentuje na Open’erze?

O tym przekonamy się już 1 lipca…

items.body:
TV Guide Editors Oct. 27, 2026 at 10:09 a.m. PT It's been scientifically proven that there is no better time of year than this one to get cozy in front of the TV and watch a really good show. Luckily, November has plenty of options for you, including returning favorites like Julian Fellowes' fizzy period drama The Gilded Age, last season's best new network comedy The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins, and the fantasy series The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power. New shows this month include the Rose Byrne-Meghann Fahy limited series The Good Daughter; the Amy Poehler comedy Dig; and the latest addition to the Blade Runner franchise, Blade Runner 2099. There's a little something for everyone.

Our guide to the best TV and streaming movies in November is divided into three sections: the best shows to watch this month, the best shows to watch by streaming service, and a calendar of TV highlights. Whatever you're looking for, you'll find it below.

Christmas is coming early to Netflix this year, and I'm not just talking about the blizzard of holiday movies hitting the streamer in November (there's a movie coming called Rodeo Christmas Romance, which is basically a Hallmark Christmas movie word cloud come to life). The month sees several interesting releases heading your way from all types of genres, from an awkward fraudster romance limited series to a supernatural thriller about a Catholic high school dance team to a bisexual Texas women crime story (that's The Altruists, the new series The Body, and The Hunting Wives Season 2, in that order). Also coming are new seasons of the charming Inuit comedy North of North and the spy thriller Black Doves, as well as the Netflix original film The Mosquito Bowl, which stars Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgård, and Ray Nicholson as college football stars who enlist in the Marines during World War II. And for those who missed it in theaters or on Peacock, Curry Barker 's box office hit Obsession comes to Netflix on Nov. 17. Here's our list of the best shows and movies on Netflix in November, plus everything coming to and leaving Netflix in November.

One of the crown jewels in the acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Skydance is undoubtedly HBO, but since the merger was completed in early October, HBO has been pretty quiet. Last month's trickle of interesting new releases continues in November, with the month's big new debut being Season 4 of Julian Fellowes' period drama The Gilded Age. But it should be a good one, with plenty of lingering threads to tie up following a tremendous Season 3 finale. Also coming in…

items.summary: Hulu confirmed it on 16 November, days before the season 4 finale airs on 24 November.
items.matters: Hulu is committing to its Emayatzy Corinealdi-led drama before it knows how season 4 ends.
items.body:
Apple TV's Slow Horses is flying out of the gate when it comes to renewals. The spy drama just wrapped up its sixth season, was previously renewed for seventh and eighth seasons, and now will stick around for Seasons 9 and 10. This will easily make it Apple TV's longest-running series, which is even more impressive considering Apple TV launched in 2019 and Slow Horses Season 1 premiered in 2022.

Elsewhere, HBO renewed Youth, Sharon Horgan's semi-autobiographical series about a divorcée's search for love and sex, for a second season. Netflix is bringing back Nobody Wants This, the rom-com about a rabbi who falls in love with an agnostic podcaster, for a fourth season. And Adults, the FX comedy about a group of friends sharing a house in New York City, has finally been renewed for a supersized third season, which is great news for the viewers who were left wondering about its future after Season 2 premiered in September.

On the drama side, Netflix has a new longest-running scripted series: Ahead of its Season 8 premiere, Virgin River was renewed for a record-breaking ninth season.

As the fall TV season winds down, check back here throughout the month for the latest news. We're keeping tabs on all the shows that have been canceled or renewed in November below.

items.headline: Commission preliminarily finds Temu in breach of the DSA over illegal product sales (new findings, 17 November)
items.summary: it cites weak product-compliance checks, weak content moderation and an ineffective sanction system. This follows the €200m fine in May and the action plan accepted on 26 October.
items.matters: if you run a marketplace or take third-party listings, the Commission is now testing your moderation and sanction systems, not only your risk assessment.
items.body:
The European Commission preliminarily found Temu in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA) obligation to put in place reasonable, proportionate and effective measures to mitigate the risk of illegal products being offered on its platform.

The Commission preliminarily found that Temu's mitigation measures include ineffective controls to check the compliance of products; a weak content moderation system; and an ineffective sanction system.

Shopping online should not mean risking the purchase of illegal and unsafe products. Under the Digital Services Act, platforms are responsible for protecting users from the risk of illegal content and goods. The preliminary findings against Temu mark another step towards making the online world safer.

items.headline: Commission preliminarily finds TikTok's For You feed in breach of the DSA (6 November)
items.summary: the recommender can repeatedly push users, including minors, towards content about sadness, isolation or body image. The findings cover risk assessment and mitigation.
items.matters: recommender design is now being judged as a systemic risk, so ranking and personalisation logic needs a documented risk assessment.
items.body:
The European Commission has preliminarily found TikTok in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA) for the so-called ‘rabbit hole effect’ of its recommender system.

TikTok's ‘For You' feed shows users a continuous stream of personalised videos, even when those are related to mental health struggles and body image.

The more a user interacts with a certain type of content, the more TikTok's ‘For You' feed algorithm recommends similar content. This design can be harmful when such endless and repeated exposure involves, for example, content about sadness, isolation or body image. These ‘rabbit holes' can have a detrimental impact on users' mental health, especially that of vulnerable adults and minors.

items.headline: Call for evidence on DSA advertising repository guidelines closes 2 December
items.summary: it covers searchability, targeting insights and accessibility of ad repositories for very large platforms and search engines.
items.matters: if you build ad or transparency tooling for a VLOP, this is your chance to shape the data schema before it is fixed.

items.matters: it is the Commission's own evidence base for expecting age checks in apps and services, with the blueprint as the reference implementation.
